extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies) preparing SEC registration statements/proxy and annual filing disclosures; corporate counsel, compensation committees, and disclosure/compliance personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and instructions for preparing Item 402 (Executive Compensation) disclosure in SEC registration statements, annual reports and proxy/information statements, including the Compensation Discussion & Analysis, Summary Compensation Table, Grants of Plan-Based Awards table, and related narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign private issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign private issuer will be deemed to comply with this Item if it provides the information required by Items 6.B, 6.E.2, and 6.F of Form 20-F, with more detailed information provided if otherwise made publicly available or required to be disclosed by the issuer's home jurisdiction or a market in which its securities are listed or traded, or paragraph (19) of General Instruction B of Form 40-F, as applicable. A foreign private issuer that elects to provide domestic Item 402 disclosure must provide the disclosure required by Item 402(w) in its annual report or registration statement, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: All compensation covered
rubrics_metrics.description: This Item requires clear, concise and understandable disclosure of all plan and non-plan compensation awarded to, earned by, or paid to the named executive officers designated under paragraph (a)(3) of this Item, and directors covered by paragraph (k) of this Item, by any person for all services rendered in all capacities to the registrant and its subsidiaries, unless otherwise specifically excluded from disclosure in this Item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All such compensation shall be reported pursuant to this Item, even if also called for by another requirement, including transactions between the registrant and a third party where a purpose of the transaction is to furnish compensation to any such named executive officer or director. No amount reported as compensation for one fiscal year need be reported in the same manner as compensation for a subsequent fiscal year; amounts reported as compensation for one fiscal year may be required to be reported in a different manner pursuant to this Item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons covered (named executive officers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure shall be provided for: (i) the registrant's principal executive officer (PEO); (ii) the principal financial officer (PFO); (iii) the registrant's three most highly compensated executive officers other than the PEO and PFO who were serving as executive officers at the end of the last completed fiscal year; and (iv) up to two additional individuals for whom disclosure would have been required but who were not serving as executive officers at the end of the last completed fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of most highly compensated executive officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination is by reference to total compensation for the last completed fiscal year (as required to be disclosed pursuant to paragraph (c)(2)(x)) reduced by the amount required to be disclosed pursuant to paragraph (c)(2)(viii), provided, however, that no disclosure need be provided for any executive officer, other than the PEO and PFO, whose total compensation, as so reduced, does not exceed $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction clarifies how to calculate and the $100,000 cutoff for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of executive officer of subsidiary
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be appropriate for a registrant to include as named executive officers one or more executive officers or other employees of subsidiaries in the disclosure required by this Item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 3b-7 under the Exchange Act (17 CFR 240.3b-7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of executive officer due to overseas compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: In limited circumstances a registrant may not include in the disclosure required by this Item an individual, other than its PEO or PFO, who is one of the registrant's most highly compensated executive officers due to payment of amounts of cash compensation relating to overseas assignments attributed predominantly to such assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information for full fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PEO or PFO served in that capacity during any part of a fiscal year with respect to which information is required, information should be provided as to all of his or her compensation for the full fiscal year. If a named executive officer (other than the PEO or PFO) served as an executive officer of the registrant during any part of the fiscal year, information shall be provided as to all compensation of that individual for the full fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of table or column
rubrics_metrics.description: A table or column may be omitted if there has been no compensation awarded to, earned by, or paid to any of the named executive officers or directors required to be reported in that table or column in any fiscal year covered by that table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: stock, option, SARs, equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'stock' means instruments such as common stock, restricted stock, restricted stock units, phantom stock, phantom stock units, common stock equivalent units or any similar instruments that do not have option-like features; 'option' means instruments such as stock options, stock appreciation rights and similar instruments with option-like features; 'stock appreciation rights' ('SARs') refers to SARs payable in cash or stock, including SARs payable in cash or stock at the election of the registrant or a named executive officer; 'equity' refers generally to stock and/or options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'plan' includes any plan, contract, authorization or arrangement, whether or not set forth in any formal document, pursuant to which cash, securities, similar instruments, or any other property may be received. A plan may be applicable to one person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except with respect to paragraph (t), registrants may omit information regarding group life, health, hospitalization, or medical reimbursement plans that do not discriminate in scope, terms or operation, in favor of executive officers or directors and that are available generally to all salaried employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of incentive plan and incentive plan award
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'incentive plan' means any plan providing compensation intended to serve as incentive for performance to occur over a specified period. An 'equity incentive plan' is an incentive plan under which awards fall within FASB ASC Topic 718; a 'non-equity incentive plan' is an incentive plan that is not an equity incentive plan. 'Incentive plan award' means an award provided under an incentive plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of date of grant/grant date
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms 'date of grant' or 'grant date' refer to the grant date determined for financial statement reporting purposes pursuant to FASB ASC Topic 718.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of closing market price
rubrics_metrics.description: Closing market price is defined as the price at which the registrant's security was last sold in the principal United States market for such security as of the date for which the closing market price is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation Discussion and Analysis (CD&A) required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the compensation awarded to, earned by, or paid to the named executive officers. The discussion shall explain all material elements of the registrant's compensation of the named executive officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discussion shall describe: (i) the objectives of the registrant's compensation programs; (ii) what the compensation program is designed to reward; (iii) each element of compensation; (iv) why the registrant chooses to pay each element; (v) how the registrant determines the amount (and, where applicable, the formula) for each element to pay; (vi) how each compensation element and decisions regarding that element fit into overall compensation objectives and affect decisions regarding other elements; and (vii) whether and how the registrant considered the most recent shareholder advisory vote on executive compensation and how that consideration affected policies and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CD&A: examples of material information to include
rubrics_metrics.description: While material information will vary, examples may include: policies for allocating between long-term and currently paid compensation; policies allocating between cash and non-cash and among non-cash forms; basis for allocating long-term compensation among different award forms; determination of timing of awards; corporate performance items considered in setting compensation policies; structuring of compensation to reflect performance and use of discretion; structuring to reflect individual performance; policies on adjustment or recovery of awards upon restatement; factors considered in material compensation changes; how prior compensation is considered in setting other elements; basis for selecting termination/change-in-control triggers; impact of accounting and tax treatments; equity ownership requirements and hedging policies; benchmarking of compensation; and the role of executive officers in determining executive compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list is illustrative, not exhaustive; registrant should tailor CD&A to its facts and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: CD&A purpose, coverage and style instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: provide investors material information necessary to understand compensation policies and decisions regarding named executive officers. The CD&A should be of the information contained in the tables and other Item disclosures and should also cover actions regarding executive compensation taken after the registrant's last fiscal year's end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CD&A should focus on material principles underlying compensation policies and the most important factors, reflect individual circumstances of the registrant, and avoid boilerplate language and repetition of table detail. It may be necessary to discuss prior years for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential treatment for target levels and competitive harm standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are not required to disclose target levels with respect to specific quantitative or qualitative performance-related factors if disclosure would cause competitive harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard for determining competitive harm is the same standard applicable for requesting confidential treatment under Securities Act Rule 406 and Exchange Act Rule 24b-2 (incorporating Exemption 4 of FOIA). If a registrant elects not to disclose targets due to competitive harm without seeking confidential treatment, it must discuss how difficult or likely it would be for the registrant to achieve the undisclosed targets or other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-GAAP target disclosure calculation instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of target levels that are non-GAAP financial measures will not be subject to Regulation G and Item 10(e); however, disclosure must be provided as to how the number is calculated from the registrant's audited financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Compensation Table requirement (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the information specified in paragraph (c)(2) concerning the compensation of the named executive officers for each of the registrant's last three completed fiscal years, in a Summary Compensation Table in the tabular format specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table columns include Name and principal position, Year, Salary, Bonus, Stock awards, Option awards, Non-equity incentive plan compensation, Change in pension value and nonqualified deferred compensation earnings, All other compensation, and Total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and bonus reporting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The table must include the dollar value of base salary (cash and non-cash) earned by the named executive officer during the fiscal year and the dollar value of bonus (cash and non-cash) earned during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amount of salary or bonus is not calculable through the latest practicable date, include a footnote disclosing that and the expected date of determination and later disclose in an 8-K. Include amounts of salary or bonus forgone where stock or non-cash compensation was received instead (with a footnote referring to Grants of Plan-Based Awards Table).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock and option awards valuation and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards of stock, include the aggregate grant date fair value computed in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718; for options (with or without tandem SARs), include the aggregate grant date fair value computed in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a footnote disclosing all assumptions made in valuation by reference to discussion in financial statements or MD&A (deemed part of Item disclosure). If awards were repriced or materially modified during the year, include incremental fair value computed at repricing/modification date per ASC 718. For awards subject to performance conditions, report value at grant date based on probable outcome and footnote the value assuming highest performance if a lesser amount was included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-equity incentive plan compensation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the dollar value of all earnings for services performed during the fiscal year pursuant to awards under non-equity incentive plans, and all earnings on any outstanding awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the relevant performance measure is satisfied during the fiscal year, earnings are reportable for that fiscal year even if payable later. All earnings on non-equity incentive plan compensation must be identified and quantified in a footnote to the column, whether paid, payable but deferred, or payable later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in pension value and above-market earnings reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Column for change in the actuarial present value of accumulated benefit under defined benefit and actuarial pension plans from prior measurement date to current measurement date, and above-market or preferential earnings on deferred compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure applies to plans providing retirement benefits (excluding defined contribution plans). Above-market interest is interest exceeding 120% of applicable federal long-term rate (with compounding); only the above-market portion must be included. Registrant shall identify and quantify by footnote the separate amounts for pension change and above-market earnings. If pension change amount is negative, disclose by footnote but do not reflect in the sum reported in the column.

rubrics_metrics.name: All other compensation reporting (column i) and perquisites rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All other compensation not reportable elsewhere must be included in column (i), including perquisites and other personal benefits (unless aggregate amount is less than $10,000), gross-ups for tax payments, securities purchased from registrant at a discount, amounts paid in connection with termination or change-in-control, contributions to defined contribution plans, insurance premiums for life insurance, and dividends or other earnings not factored into grant date fair value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-equity incentive plan awards and earnings and earnings on stock and options (except specific exceptions) are not reportable as All Other Compensation. Benefits paid pursuant to defined benefit plans are not reportable here unless accelerated due to change-in-control. Any item reported under this paragraph that is not a perquisite and whose value exceeds $10,000 must be footnoted. Perquisites may be excluded if aggregate value is less than $10,000; if $10,000 or more, each perquisite must be identified; any perquisite exceeding greater of $25,000 or 10% of total perquisites must be quantified in a footnote and methodology for computing aggregate incremental cost described. Reimbursements of taxes with respect to perquisites must be included and quantified separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total compensation column
rubrics_metrics.description: Column (j) reports the dollar value of total compensation for the covered fiscal year — the sum of all amounts reported in columns (c) through (i) for each named executive officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for Summary Compensation Table reporting mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules: prior fiscal years' information not required if registrant was not a reporting company in that year (with exceptions); all compensation values must be in dollars and rounded to nearest dollar; reported values must be numerical single values per grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where compensation paid/received in different currency, provide a footnote identifying that currency and describe rate and methodology used to convert to dollars. If a named executive officer is also a director and receives director compensation, reflect that compensation and provide a footnote. Any amounts deferred shall be included in appropriate column for fiscal year in which earned. Reduce amounts reported in applicable column for any amounts recovered pursuant to compensation recovery policy required by listing standards and identify such amounts by footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants of plan‑based awards table requirement (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information concerning each grant of an award made to a named executive officer in the last completed fiscal year under any plan, including awards subsequently transferred, in the specified tabular format (Grants of Plan‑Based Awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table columns include Name, Grant date, Estimated future payouts under non-equity incentive plan awards (threshold/target/maximum), Estimated future payouts under equity incentive plan awards (threshold/target/maximum), All other stock awards (#), All other option awards (#), Exercise or base price, Grant date fair value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants table: required columns and their content
rubrics_metrics.description: Table shall include: name (col a); grant date for equity awards (col b); dollar value of estimated future payouts for non-equity awards (cols c-e); number of shares or option shares for equity awards (cols f-h); number of shares not required to be disclosed in cols f-h (col i); number of securities underlying options not required in f-h (col j); per-share exercise/base price (col k); grant date fair value per ASC 718 (col l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grant date differs from committee action date, add adjoining column showing such date. If exercise/base price is less than closing market price, add a column showing closing market price on date of grant. If repriced or materially modified, report incremental fair value computed at repricing/modification date in column (l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants table instructions and definitions (threshold/target/maximum etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure on a separate line for each grant; identify the particular plan for multiple-plan grants; for incentive awards, columns c-e or f-h refer to threshold (minimum payable), target (amount if specified target(s) reached or representative amount based on prior year if target not determinable), and maximum (maximum payout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If award provides only a single estimated payout, report that amount as the target. If non-equity incentive awards are denominated in units or other rights, add a column quantifying units/rights. Disclose dollar amount of consideration, if any, paid by the executive for the award in a footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise/base price methodology and tandem grants
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining if exercise/base price is less than closing market price, registrant may use either the defined closing market price or, if no market exists, any other formula prescribed for the security. Whenever exercise/base price reported is not the closing market price, describe the methodology by footnote or accompanying narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tandem grant of two instruments, only one of which is granted under an incentive plan, need be reported only in the applicable column (i or j) with the tandem feature noted by footnote or narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting repricings and material modifications in grants table
rubrics_metrics.description: Options, SARs and similar option‑like instruments granted in connection with a repricing transaction or other material modification shall be reported in this Table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, disclosure does not apply to any repricing that occurs through a pre-existing formula or mechanism in the plan or award that results in periodic adjustment of exercise/base price, an antidilution provision, or a recapitalization or similar transaction equally affecting all holders of the class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of performance‑conditioned equity awards in grants table
rubrics_metrics.description: For any equity awards that are subject to performance conditions, report in grant date fair value column the value at the grant date based upon the probable outcome of such conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amount should be consistent with the estimate of aggregate compensation cost to be recognized over the service period determined as of the grant date under ASC 718, excluding estimated forfeitures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative disclosure to summary and grants tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a narrative description of any material factors necessary to an understanding of the information disclosed in the Summary Compensation Table and the Grants of Plan-Based Awards table.
